subsystems.name: Reprogramming payload
subsystems.role: the instructions that temporarily switch skin cells back toward an embryonic-like state.
parts: mRNA encoding Oct4, Sox2 and Klf4 (the 'OSK' combination)
modified nucleosides to reduce immune reaction
cap and poly-A tail for stability

subsystems.name: Delivery vehicle
subsystems.role: carries fragile mRNA into skin cells without being destroyed first.

subsystems.name: Administration route
subsystems.role: gets the payload past the skin's outer barrier.

subsystems.name: Dose and timing control
subsystems.role: keeps reprogramming brief; continuous expression is what causes cells to lose identity or form tumours.
parts: tissue-restricted promoter or microRNA target sites
degradable mRNA with a short half-life

subsystems.name: Measurement and safety
subsystems.role: proves the epigenetic clock actually moved and that nothing dangerous happened.

buildSteps.title: Choose the factor set
buildSteps.detail: Pick which reprogramming genes to include. Dropping c-Myc reduces tumour risk but lowers efficiency, so the three-factor OSK mix is the usual starting point.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the mRNA
buildSteps.detail: Each factor's gene is transcribed in vitro into mRNA, capped and tailed, and modified nucleosides are substituted so the cell does not treat it as a viral invasion.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the lipid nanoparticles
buildSteps.detail: Lipids dissolved in ethanol are mixed with mRNA in water in a microfluidic device; the lipids self-assemble around the mRNA into particles around 100 nanometres across.

buildSteps.title: Add skin selectivity
buildSteps.detail: Particles are tuned by charge, size or surface ligands, or paired with a microneedle array, so the payload reaches fibroblasts and keratinocytes rather than the liver.

buildSteps.title: Test on human skin models
buildSteps.detail: Lab-grown skin and donated skin explants are treated, then methylation-clock assays check whether cells look younger while still behaving like skin cells.

buildSteps.title: Move to animal testing
buildSteps.detail: Mice receive repeated doses to measure clock reversal, wound healing and hair regrowth, with careful checks for teratomas or cells drifting toward a stem-like state.

buildSteps.title: Fix the dosing schedule
buildSteps.detail: Short pulses spaced apart are tested to find the shortest exposure that resets the clock, since longer expression erases cell identity.

buildSteps.title: Assess safety and durability
buildSteps.detail: Long-term animal studies check whether the effect persists for months, whether immune responses build up against the lipid or the mRNA, and whether any treated patch turns abnormal.

buildSteps.title: Run human trials
buildSteps.detail: If safety holds, small first-in-human studies would treat a defined skin area, take biopsies, and compare methylation age and tissue structure before and after.

prerequisites.why: the Yamanaka factors were shown to turn adult cells into stem-like cells in 2006, which is the whole basis of the idea.
modified-nucleoside mRNA in lipid particles is already used in licensed vaccines, proving the delivery chemistry works.

prerequisites.tech: Partial, reversible reprogramming in living animals
prerequisites.why: mouse studies have reversed age-related changes, including restoring vision, using cyclic factor expression, but only in animals.

prerequisites.tech: Delivery that targets skin instead of liver
prerequisites.why: injected lipid nanoparticles concentrate in the liver; reliable, safe skin targeting is not yet solved.
methylation clocks are validated as research measures but are not accepted regulators' proof of a clinical benefit.
no reliable method yet guarantees that no treated cell keeps dividing or becomes cancerous.

pathway.milestone: animal and cell-culture studies showing partial clock reversal in skin without obvious harm
pathway.unlocks: evidence the approach is worth pursuing in humans.

pathway.milestone: non-viral, skin-targeted delivery with pulsed dosing validated in human skin explants and primates
first-in-human safety trials on a small skin patch, with biopsy-measured methylation age
pathway.unlocks: knowing whether the effect transfers from mice to people.

pathway.milestone: regulated local treatments for skin ageing or wounds, if safety data holds up over years
pathway.unlocks: rejuvenation as a controlled medical procedure rather than a whole-body experiment, which remains much riskier.
